items.question: A truck and a bicycle are both moving at 20 mph. Which has more kinetic energy?
options: The truck, because it has more mass
The bicycle, because it is lighter
They have the same energy because they're moving at the same speed
items.correct_answer: The truck, because it has more mass
items.explanation: Kinetic energy depends on both mass and speed. At the same speed, an object with more mass has more kinetic energy.

items.question: You roll two balls down a ramp - a heavy metal ball and a light plastic ball - at the same speed. At the bottom, they each hit a block. The metal ball pushes the block farther. Use evidence about energy to explain why.

rubric.4: Explains that heavier ball has more kinetic energy at same speed, more energy transferred to block, causing greater movement
rubric.3: Connects mass and energy with some explanation of transfer
rubric.2: Mentions mass affecting outcome but energy explanation incomplete
rubric.1: States metal ball is heavier without energy connection

items.question: A metal spoon sitting in hot soup becomes warm. What type of energy transfer is this?
options: Heat energy moving from the soup to the spoon
Light energy moving from the spoon to the soup
items.correct_answer: Heat energy moving from the soup to the spoon
items.explanation: Heat energy transfers from warmer objects to cooler objects. The hot soup transfers heat to the cooler metal spoon.

items.question: Energy can be transferred in different ways: by sound, light, heat, and electric currents. Give one real-world example of each type of energy transfer. Explain how the energy moves from one place to another in each example.

rubric.4: Four correct examples with clear explanation of energy movement for each (e.g., sun to Earth for light, heater to room for heat)
rubric.3: Four examples with explanation for most
rubric.2: Some examples correct with partial explanations
rubric.1: Few examples without clear energy transfer explanation

items.question: Two billiard balls collide. Ball A was moving fast, Ball B was still. After collision, Ball A slows down and Ball B starts moving. What happened to the energy?
options: Energy transferred from Ball A to Ball B
Energy was created in Ball B
items.correct_answer: Energy transferred from Ball A to Ball B
items.explanation: When objects collide, energy transfers between them. The moving ball transfers some of its kinetic energy to the stationary ball.

items.question: You drop a ball from 1 meter high. It bounces back up but not quite as high as where it started. Ask two questions about what happened to the energy. Then, predict what would happen if you dropped the ball from 2 meters instead.

rubric.4: Two investigable questions about energy loss (friction, sound, heat) and correct prediction that ball bounces higher but still loses some energy
rubric.2: Questions or prediction present but not both developed

items.question: A solar-powered calculator converts energy from what form to what form?
items.explanation: Solar panels convert light energy from the sun into electrical energy that powers the calculator.

items.question: Design a device that converts one form of energy to another useful form. Draw your device and label: 1) What energy goes IN, 2) What energy comes OUT, 3) How the conversion happens. Explain a problem your device could solve.

rubric.4: Creative device with clear input/output energy labeled, mechanism explained, and practical problem solved
rubric.3: Device with energy conversion shown and some explanation
rubric.2: Device drawn but energy conversion unclear

items.question: A wave with a large amplitude compared to a wave with a small amplitude will:
items.explanation: A wave's amplitude is related to its energy. Larger amplitude means the wave carries more energy.

items.question: Draw two waves: one with HIGH amplitude and one with LOW amplitude. Draw two more waves: one with LONG wavelength and one with SHORT wavelength. Label all parts. Explain how a loud sound is different from a quiet sound using wave properties.

rubric.4: Four correctly drawn waves with labels, clear explanation connecting amplitude to loudness
rubric.3: Waves drawn correctly with some explanation
rubric.2: Some waves correct or explanation incomplete

items.question: When you look in a mirror, you see your reflection. What is happening to the light?
options: Light bounces off the mirror back to your eyes
Light is absorbed by the mirror
New light is created by the mirror
items.correct_answer: Light bounces off the mirror back to your eyes
items.explanation: Mirrors reflect light. Light bounces off the smooth surface of the mirror and travels back to your eyes, allowing you to see a reflection.

items.question: Create a model showing how you see an apple on a table. Draw: 1) the light source, 2) the apple, 3) your eye, and 4) arrows showing how light travels. Explain what happens to the light at each step.

rubric.4: Complete model with light source, arrows to apple, reflection off apple to eye, with clear explanation of light path
rubric.3: Model with most components and partial explanation
rubric.2: Some components shown but light path incomplete

items.question: A lighthouse uses flashing light patterns to send messages to ships. Which pattern best represents the message 'SOS' in Morse code (... --- ...)?
items.explanation: Information can be encoded in patterns of light. Different patterns represent different messages, just like Morse code.

items.question: Design your own code system using light or sound patterns to send secret messages to a friend. Create a code for at least 5 letters or words. Explain how your system works and why it is effective for communication.

rubric.4: Creative, consistent code system with 5+ symbols, clear explanation of how sender and receiver use it, and why patterns work for communication
rubric.2: Some code elements but system incomplete
rubric.1: Idea present but not a working code

items.question: A cactus has thick stems that store water. How does this internal structure help the cactus survive?
options: It allows the cactus to live in dry desert environments
It helps the cactus move to find water
It protects the cactus from sunlight
It helps the cactus communicate with other plants
items.correct_answer: It allows the cactus to live in dry desert environments
items.explanation: Internal structures have specific functions. The cactus's water-storing stems help it survive in dry environments where water is scarce.

items.question: Compare the structures of a fish and a bird. Identify at least two external structures and one internal structure for each animal. Explain how these structures help each animal survive in its environment.

rubric.4: Multiple structures for each animal (fins/wings, scales/feathers, gills/lungs) with clear function and environment connection
rubric.3: Structures identified for both with some functional explanation
rubric.2: Some structures but connection to survival incomplete

items.question: A rabbit sees a hawk flying overhead and immediately runs to hide. What is the order of events in the rabbit's response?
options: Eyes detect hawk → brain processes danger → legs run
Legs run → brain thinks → eyes see
Brain processes → nothing happens → ears hear
items.correct_answer: Eyes detect hawk → brain processes danger → legs run
items.explanation: Animals receive information through senses, the brain processes the information, and then the body responds appropriately.

items.question: Create a model showing how a dog responds when it smells food. Include: 1) the sensory receptor, 2) how the brain processes the information, and 3) how the dog responds. Use arrows to show the flow of information.

rubric.4: Complete model with nose (receptor), brain (processing), body response (moving toward food), arrows showing information flow
rubric.3: Model with main components and some flow explanation
rubric.2: Some components shown but information flow unclear
rubric.1: Simple drawing without information processing shown

items.question: Scientists find a rock layer with sea shells on top of a mountain. What evidence does this provide about Earth's past?
options: The mountain was once under the ocean
Someone put the shells there recently
items.correct_answer: The mountain was once under the ocean
items.explanation: Rock layers and fossils provide evidence of past environments. Sea shell fossils on a mountain indicate that area was once an ocean floor.

items.question: You are studying rock layers in a canyon. The bottom layer has fish fossils, the middle layer has fern fossils, and the top layer has no fossils but shows cracks. Describe how the environment in this area changed over time. Use evidence from each layer.

rubric.4: Explains environmental changes chronologically: ocean (fish) → swamp/forest (ferns) → dry land (cracks), using all evidence
rubric.3: Most environments correctly identified with evidence
rubric.2: Some environments identified but sequence or evidence weak
rubric.1: Recognizes layers but doesn't interpret environment

items.question: Over many years, a river carves a canyon through rock. What process is most responsible for this change?
items.explanation: Flowing water slowly erodes rock over time, carrying small pieces away. Over millions of years, this creates canyons.

items.question: Design an investigation to test how the speed of water affects erosion. What materials would you use? What would you measure? What do you predict you would observe?

rubric.4: Complete investigation with materials (soil, trays, water), controlled variables, measurement plan (amount eroded), and prediction (faster water = more erosion)
rubric.2: Basic investigation idea but variables or measurement unclear
rubric.1: Mentions water and erosion but no investigation plan

items.question: Looking at a topographic map, you see many lines close together in one area. What does this pattern indicate?
items.explanation: On topographic maps, lines close together indicate rapid elevation change - a steep slope. Lines far apart show flat areas.

items.question: Burning coal releases energy, but also causes pollution. This is an example of how using natural resources:
options: Has both benefits and drawbacks for the environment
Has no effect on the environment
items.correct_answer: Has both benefits and drawbacks for the environment
items.explanation: Using natural resources like fossil fuels provides energy but can harm the environment through pollution.

items.question: Earthquakes can damage buildings and hurt people. Compare TWO different solutions for reducing earthquake damage: 1) Building codes requiring stronger buildings, and 2) Early warning systems. What are the pros and cons of each?

rubric.4: Both solutions analyzed with pros and cons (cost, effectiveness, accessibility), reasoned comparison
rubric.3: Both solutions with some pros and cons for each
rubric.2: One solution well-analyzed or both superficially

items.question: A school wants to design a new playground. Which criteria would be MOST important for success?
options: Safety, fun for students, and fits in available space
It should be the tallest in the state
It should have only one type of equipment
It should use materials that rust quickly
items.correct_answer: Safety, fun for students, and fits in available space
items.explanation: Design criteria are the requirements for success. A playground needs to be safe, enjoyable, and fit within space constraints.

items.question: Your community needs a way to reduce plastic waste. Generate three possible solutions. Compare them based on: 1) How well it reduces waste, 2) How easy it is to implement, and 3) How much it costs. Recommend the best solution.

rubric.4: Three creative solutions with systematic comparison across all three criteria, well-reasoned recommendation
rubric.3: Three solutions with comparison and recommendation

items.question: Students tested egg-drop containers. They recorded: Design A - egg broke, Design B - egg cracked slightly, Design C - egg was unharmed. Design A used foam, Design B used paper, Design C used foam with bubble wrap inside. What can you conclude from this test? What variables should be controlled for a fair test?

rubric.4: Correct conclusion about materials protecting egg, identifies key variables (drop height, egg size, container size) and explains importance of control
rubric.3: Good conclusions with some variables identified
